Kyle, saw Lumos launch the Identity Agent Force to govern access across human, machine, and AI identities.

A launch that ambitious usually opens more in-market accounts than an emerging-enterprise team can cover before they cool, and that is where good deals slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Lumos off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress around 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Kyle, quick follow-up for Lumos.

With a major product moment, demand on the emerging-enterprise segment jumps faster than rep capacity, and most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to hit the number. The gap shows up late, and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your segment needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Kyle, last bit of proof for Lumos.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Lumos's reply rate likely compares to peer identity-security startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an emerging-enterprise motion? I will tailor it to Lumos either way.
